item.title: (no title)
item.content:encoded:
Thank you for the upvote, MacLeod. I'm quite aware of your dislike of the 012 article (and I share yours and Kalinin's opinion—it's a bad article). I fully expected a downvote from you for that reason. So, getting an upvote from you means a lot to me.

But yes, as Decibelle said, I don't think I've done anything to keep 012 around. It's over +100. It's in Containment Breach. Believe me, if I could rewrite it, I totally would. Furthermore, I know that if it descended to the negatives, it would be rewritten, if not by me then by someone. It would not be simply deleted. 012 will stay, whatever my efforts are or not.

012 is in such a strange space. The article is spotty and poorly constructed. It can be simplified to something what crazies you to death. However, there's a core, a soul to the article that is compelling. I want to explore it. I'm driven to deconstruct the barebones structure and infuse the life within it that we can see should be there.

The 012 article is kind of like 012 itself.

item.title: (no title)
item.content:encoded:
Staying with me in my room are two other Americans, Anderson and Spitzer. They arrived together, and work together back in the States. They say that they're going to clear out the National Library, see what texts can be salvaged.

Spitzer's also a Foundation agent. Anderson's earlier statement about Spitzer being exposed to the quarto was further evidence of their relationship. Yes, I'm writing without directly linking to SCP-701, but the implied backstory is that Anderson and Spitzer are in Florence to recover a 1640 quarto of SCP-701. The flood is just the opportunity.

"All the best": …That should have been "All for the best." Will fix.

And yes, 7/12 time (which is actually a thing, in short bits) is deliberate. Partly because 012 is a "disagreeable cacophony," and partly because there's an in-world Easter egg there. (Also, I can write copious amounts of insane numerology.)

I'll review the events of 14 and 15, make sure it's clear enough what's going on.

I'm not good with colors, though. I was hoping for a darker red, but didn't know how to make it.

But all in all, I'm just glad that I could take this line:

SCP-012 was retrieved by Archaeologist K.M. Sandoval during the excavation of a northern Italian tomb destroyed in a recent storm.

and connect it to important real-life events. It also was the great source of the photos (photos of the aftermath of the 1966 Florence flood are public domain from the Italian government, the photo of the 1966 Leonids is from NASA, and the music is from Beethoven's notes).

item.title: (no title)
item.content:encoded:
It's interesting to see the number of people who want this idea to do well, but are nervous about the difficulty of execution. I would also put myself in that category, despite being quite keen to write for the canon if inspiration strikes.

I was pleased with the result here overall. The middle section in particular is evocative and engaging, and doesn't tip its hand too early in relation to insanity. I also like that it provides backstory without completely settling matters - there's at least one more story to tell.

I feel like the opening section has slightly too many "he"s and "she"s, as well as "he asks", "he says" - it feels a bit static.

8-13 November entries are the ones I particularly like - great photos and I'm not too maxed out on purple to find the prose cliche.

In 12 November, I think "our late composer's" is too early - he would just be a "late musician" as the contents of the papers are unknown.

For 14 November, presumably the reference to 7/12 meter (which does not compute in standard Western musical notation) is deliberate. I didn't quite understand the interaction here - Spitzer mutters something about containment, but Anderson is later revealed as the Foundation agent. Also "All the best" made no sense to me.

As 15 November is a "cheat" diary where the writer appears to write in the middle of acting, I suggest that it not have a picture. I think you can use this picture (which is great) for 13 November (which is not as strong). "He has locked the door"- I couldn't work out whether that was Spitzer or Anderson. Finally, I would lose the paragraph about karate - that felt odd, partly because I thought Spitzer was handcuffed to the bed, and partly because Asian martial art names don't fit the purple prose. Presumably KM can simply steal the key and hide it for later.

In 16 November, I would be tempted to make the red colour slightly darker.

item.content:encoded:
You could write a long and epic and sprawling tale and include a three-word throwaway where someone burned 012 to ashes, just out of spite, and 012 would probably still gain votes. It'll be one of those skips that continues to gain votes no matter what happens.

I think re-contextualizing a (from the POV of the person writing the tale) shitty skip and turning it into something better isn't a bad thing. In fact, people have done that with stuff like 343, 105, 076, 049, 106, 682, 173, 2000, etc. etc., even the goddamn Jester. I think being doubtful that a tale based off a skip you don't like is valid, but to say that writing about it is fruitless seems defeatist to me.

Excellent feedback. Thank you, Kalinin.

Part of it is that I wanted to help establish the mood of the series. It is going to be a bit more Lovecraftian and/or Gothic in its style than most SCP tales, so, yes, the journal's a bit more florid on purpose. It's part of why the concept was well received, and I'm going to keep it going. It's not everyone's style, I'm well aware, but as the stories develop, we'll keep your concerns about the content in mind.

item.title: (no title)
item.content:encoded:
Using SCP-012 as the starting point for a major project seems problematic to me. That's part of a more general issue I have when people expend lots of energy and effort trying to invest thin or boring starting concepts with meaning and interest. Frequently, you end up with something that's better-written than the original, but ultimately it's still uninteresting.

This is apparently the start of something ongoing, so time will tell if this work as a whole falls into that trap. This particular installment isn't really pointing the way to much beyond the boundaries of the original article (an article that's not very good, FWIW). Really, this amounts to an extremely detailed recovery log and testing log interspersed with some commentary. The only real new information is the fact that it's close to being finished, but that's still within the boundaries of the original concept. It's not really making me reconsider the original premise or making it feel much different to me.

The writing itself is okay, though the language in the journal entries is a little florid. I suppose that can be chalked up to the fact that this guy has at least a little antiquarian in him, but it reads very much like a standard-issue Lovecraftian "guy what goes crazy" narrative. That might not have been a problem in and of itself, but the narrative arc of the journals has already been described in the original article and I'm expecting it, and there it is being dutifully carried out.

I may reevaluate this upon subsequent works, but right now, I'm not seeing why 012 is worth the effort, which I think should be one of the main points of this project you're working on.

item.title: It begins.
item.content:encoded:
This is a collaboration between LadyKatie and myself. It's been a while in coming, and it's a starting point for the On Mount Golgotha canon.

So, where did SCP-012 come from? What does it mean? Why does it exist? We're going to explore and find out.
